topic: Eight losing weeks: what history says, and what to check
caption:
Eight straight weekly falls — the Nifty 50's longest losing run in 25 years. It closed at 22,421.95 on 1 October after a 3.11% week, around 15% below its January high of 26,373.

Some history, because it is rarer than it feels. The last streak this long was 2001, at nine weeks. The longest on record is ten weeks, in 1993. Every one of them ended, and not one announced it beforehand — which is context, not a forecast. A 20% fall from a peak is what's conventionally called a bear market, and the index has not reached that.

Four things worth checking while the headlines are loud: whether your asset mix has drifted from your target, whether any goal date has moved closer, whether your emergency fund is still untouched, and whether your SIP instalments are still going through.

One piece of arithmetic: the same instalment buys more units when prices are lower. That only helps someone who keeps paying it.

Sources: market reports and index levels, 1–2 October 2026.
For education only. Not investment advice.
